# Workflow Conventions

## One combined ci-cd.yml

CI (build/test) and release (publish/tag) live in one workflow, `ci-cd.yml`, with a single workflow-level concurrency block — `group: ci-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}` — and zero per-job blocks: superseded runs on the same branch cancel whole, while `main` runs queue (overlapping release merges wait their turn), so `publish-stable` can never die mid-release. Triggers: `push: [main, dev]`, `pull_request: [dev]`, `workflow_dispatch` — no `workflow_run` (one file means `needs` is the green gate) and no `pull_request: [main]` (the standing release PR's head already ran identical CI via the dev push; it reports zero checks, and `main` branch protection must require none). CI jobs are gated `if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'`; `publish-stable` runs on `main` push; `publish-dev` runs on `dev` push after the DAG sinks; `ensure-release-pr` runs on `dev` push with no `needs` (it consumes no CI output).

The job DAG (`check` is the root; `publish-dev` needs the sinks; `needs` is transitive — ancestors are never re-listed):

```
mirror → check → docker-matrix → build-docker → publish-compose
          check → unity-matrix → unity-check
```

`mirror` preceding `check` is the one deliberate exception to check-as-root: the repo-specific preflight builds the postgres wrapper image, whose `FROM` is a mirror-prefixed base from `workloads/images.lock`, so the mirror namespace must be populated before `check` pulls from it — and because `check` needs `mirror`, a cycle is forbidden, making `mirror` the one parallel root. `publish-dev` needs `[publish-compose, unity-check]`.

## Shared devkit operations: uvx for release-devkit, inline `uv run` for the rest

Shared devkit operations split by consumption model. release-devkit cannot be a project dependency (it sits inside every consumer's own dependency graph), so its verbs run as inlined `uvx --from release-devkit==${{ env.RELEASE_DEVKIT_VERSION }}` steps, version-pinned in the workflow `env:` — see release-devkit's `AGENTS.md` for the consumption shape (including the ledger-checkout law: `fetch-depth: 0` + `fetch-tags: true` for every ledger-reading job, `persist-credentials: false` except `publish-stable`). The `check` job ends with `publish-stable --dry-run` (the publish-plan gate). unity-devkit is a PyPI dev-group dependency like the others, so its verbs run inline as `uv run` (version-sourced by `uv.lock`): `unity-matrix` runs `uv run compile-check-unity-matrix` (emitting the include matrix plus the license tag), and each `unity-check` leg runs `uv run compile-check-unity` inside its `matrix.editor-image` `unityci/editor` container on self-hosted `unity` runners — license restore-or-activate and the UPM cache are verb-internal. Every other devkit (`python-devkit`, `docker-devkit`, `openapi-client-codegen`) is a PyPI dependency the same way: `mirror` runs `uv run mirror`; the `check` job runs `uv run preflight-python` (the python battery) then `uv run preflight` (repo-specific checks) then `uv run generate-clients --check` (openapi staleness gate); `docker-matrix` runs `uv run docker-build-matrix` (one entry per variant, targets grouped by dependency closure — dependents with the base their `additional_contexts: target:` references pull in); `build-docker` and `publish-compose` run repo-local scripts (`build-docker --variant ${{ matrix.variant }} --targets ${{ matrix.targets }}` per leg, QEMU kept). Inline jobs use `astral-sh/setup-uv@v7` with cache restore (`save-cache: "true"` only in `check` — matrix legs and one-shot jobs never race concurrent cache saves). Every `uv run` auto-syncs the environment to what it needs — no `--no-sync` anywhere: the battery's full sync (`--all-packages --extra cpu`, from the `[tool.python-devkit.preflight]` table) is battery-internal, consumed by its own basedpyright/pytest steps, and everything after it re-syncs its own context anyway (`preflight`'s inner `uv run generate-datamodels`; `generate-clients`' per-project spec dumps, `spec_command: uv run --project .`).

## PyPI matrix eliminated — one `release` environment

Both PyPI packages (`placeframe-common`, `placeframe-core-python`) publish from the single `publish-stable` job (and the single `publish-dev` job) under one shared `release` environment — no per-package matrix. PyPI's OIDC trusted-publishing `GitHubPublisher` row is keyed by `(owner, repo, workflow_filename, environment)` and linked to projects many-to-many (`project.oidc_publishers`); concrete publishers (established packages) are reused across projects, so one publisher `(placeframe, ci-cd.yml, release)` validates for both packages. The earlier per-package `pypi-<project>` environments and `--only`/`--exclude` splits were based on the disproven "one project per tuple" reading and are gone. The `release` environment carries no protection rules — the `dev` → `main` release-PR is the human gate, which is what lets the dev channel share it without an approval gate (if `release` ever gains required reviewers, the dev channel breaks). CI jobs have no environment. npm trusted publishers are bound to `ci-cd.yml` (one publisher per package, single workflow filename). `publish-stable` passes `--fetch-ci-artifacts` to staple CI build outputs onto the GitHub Release; `create-release` runs inside the command whenever something published.

All workflow logic lives in Python scripts (release-devkit commands via `uvx --from`, repo-local scripts via `uv run`) — no inline shell conditionals or loops.
